newsitem.title: USA: Continental Cable, Cisco in Internet pact.
newsitem.headline: Continental Cable, Cisco in Internet pact.

text.p: Continental Cablevision, the U.S. cable TV operating arm of U S West Media Group, and Cisco Systems Inc said Monday they planned to conduct trials of Cisco's most advanced Internet technologies.

The companies said they would test technologies to deliver broadband Internet applications and services, including high capacity streaming video, telephony over the Internet (IP telephony) and interactive games.
The also said they had agreed to a marketing deal that will make Cisco networking products and support available to Continental customers as part of a one-stop shopping effort.

They said trials of Cisco's new router technologies, capable of switching data between networks at more than one billion bit-per-second speeds, will begin in 1997. The tests are designed to help both companies understand the demands of customers using broadband Internet applications and services.
Cable modem and digital subscriber line (DSL) access technologies will be used in the efforts, the companies said.
Continental also will be among the first broadband Internet providers to use Cisco's telecommunications carrier-class gigabit switching routers, they said.
